It has no Start, Fame, Repeatable, Previous or Expansion field, so gates.fame is all null, gates.prev is [], gates.expansion is null and gates.repeatable is null unless the page says otherwise in words -- null here is 'the field does not exist on this template', not 'false'. start.raw is the header's own NPC Name / Zone / pos values joined, because there is no single Start string to quote.

CAMPAIGN RANK 'Bronze Ribbon of Service' is a real access gate with no schema field. It is NOT gates.level, which means character level and which this header gives as 'Any' -> null. Flagged rank_gate_unmodelled.

THE PAGE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE GRID REF. The header Description says 'Travel to Ruhotz Silvermines via North Gustaberg (K-9)'; walkthrough bullet 2 says the Allied Ensign is at (K-8). I used (K-8): bullet 2 is the line giving the instruction, and it is the only one naming the entity you actually interact with. The sibling page Brave Dawn III (B) (cached page 0022605) writes the same landmark as 'east-(K-8)', which agrees with bullet 2 -- I record that as corroboration only; this page's own bullet 2 is what I read. Flagged grid_conflict, and that conflict is why this is medium.

TIME. Header says 'Time: 30 min'; Notes[1] says 'There seems to be no time limit to how long you can take to get to Ruhotz Silvermines.' Read as a player, those are not the same claim -- the note is scoped to the journey, the header is the battlefield clock -- so I did not treat it as a flat contradiction, but the page never says which clock the 30 minutes is on. Recorded, not modelled: there is no time field.

THE SOLDIER IS NOT A STEP AND NOT A TARGET. Bullet 4 introduces 'a Soldier' who runs at the crab on his own; the sub-bullets are the focus messages ('unfocused', 'training harder', 'fighting with vigor') and bullet 5's sub-bullets are tactics plus the fail condition. None of that is something you go and do, and the page gives the Soldier no position, so he is described in the note on step 3 rather than given a rung.

THIS OP ENDS TWICE, and the difference from its siblings is load-bearing. Bullet 5 says 'Exit via Dawn Aureola' -- a battlefield exit that Brave Dawn III (B) does not mention at all -- and bullet 6 says 'Return and talk to Hieronymus for your reward'. Both are steps; dropping the second would leave the player unmarked for the hand-in.

NO EVIDENCE anywhere: no key item changes hands and the rewards are experience points and Allied Notes, neither of which is in inventory.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 2: See grid_conflict in the record note.

start.raw: NPC Name: Hieronymus | Zone: Bastok Markets (S) | pos: E-8

steps.note: accept the op from the Campaign Ops NPC named in the header.

Zone out of Bastok Markets (S) and follow the wall east. Bullet 3 the party leader selects to enter and you are transported into Ruhotz Silvermines is the same interaction, not a separate rung. The header Description puts this at (K-9); bullet 2 says (K-8) and I used (K-8).

inside the battlefield. An allied NPC Soldier engages the Trained Crab on his own; you assist. The page's tactic is to let him tank until he is 'fighting with vigor' and then attack, and bullet 5's sub-bullet warns that if he never gains focus you LOSE the op. Notes[3]/[4] add that the crab shifts hate often and has roughly 8000-10000 HP. Target is none because the crab is carried in mobs; the Soldier is not a target -- the page gives him no name and no position.

bullet 5's second sentence: 'Exit via Dawn Aureola.' Kept as its own rung because it is an instruction with a named, targetable exit, and because it is exactly the line that distinguishes this op from Brave Dawn III (B), which ends the battlefield with no exit sentence at all.
'Return and talk to Hieronymus for your reward.' The op is not complete at the kill.

REPEATABLE IS SET, AND ONLY BECAUSE THE PAGE SAYS SO IN WORDS. Notes[1]: 'This is repeatable (as long as you have tags), making it a very quick and easy way to stock up on Allied Notes.' That is a statement about the op, not a header field, so gates.repeatable is true here while it stays null on the pages in this batch that say nothing.

THREE RUNGS, NOT FOUR. Bullets 2 and 3 are one conversation with the Adjutant: he asks which craft you specialise in, then quizzes you on TWO synths (the crystal and the first through fourth ingredients, the fourth marked optional). A quiz answered in a menu is not a place you travel to, and two consecutive rungs on the same NPC are one marker anyway, so bullet 3 is folded into step 2.

THE ADJUTANT'S ZONE IS INFERRED, and I am saying so rather than letting it default. Bullet 1 and the header Description give only a grid ref, '(J-9)'. A step left with no zone silently inherits the giver's, so guessing wrong and asserting nothing look the same downstream. I asserted Bastok Markets (S): the player is standing in front of Hieronymus at (E-8) in Bastok Markets (S) when he is 'forwarded' to (J-9), and the sibling page Stock and Awe III (B) (cached page 0022454) spells its own forwarded NPC as the wikilink [[Quartermaster - Bastok Markets (S)|Quartermaster]], which is direct evidence that these secondary Campaign Ops NPCs stand in the giver's own city zone. That fact came from that page, not this one. Flagged npc_zone_inferred.

NOT STEPS: bullet 1's 'Easily'/reward framing, Notes[2] (a comparison to Crystal Fist I (B)), and the whole 'Recipes' section, which is an unconverted wikitable whose every row still reads 'Item name / Ingredients' -- a blank template, not content.

THE ZONE CHOICE IS AN OR AND IS NOT MODELLED. Bullet 2 says 'go to a Bastokan controlled Campaign area'; bullet 3 lists exactly two -- North Gustaberg (S) (F-7) and Grauberg (S) (L-4) -- and bullet 5 pairs each with its destination NPC. You do ONE. `group` would be a different and false claim ('do all of these in any order'), so I modelled the North Gustaberg (S) pair, which is the first listed and the one adjacent to Bastok Markets (S), and recorded the Grauberg (S) pair in the step notes. A player who picks Grauberg gets a marker on the other valid option, not on a wrong place. Flagged or_branch_unmodelled.

THE DESTINATION IS NAMED, so nothing generic is needed. The prose calls it 'the Campaign NPC' -- in the wikitext that is the category link [[:Category:Campaign NPC|Campaign NPC]], which is a category and not a name -- but bullet 5 then gives the real ones: Jagged Onyx, L.C. at (D-10) in North Gustaberg (S) and Polished Fang, L.C. at (I-8) in Grauberg (S). Those are what I wrote.

THE ESCORT IS FOLDED INTO THE ARRIVAL. Bullet 4 is the escort itself; it has no place of its own -- the Reinforcement starts beside the Gate Sentry you just talked to, so a separate rung would put a second marker on the rung above it. The markable thing is where you are taking him. Bullets 4, 5 and 6 are therefore one step.

NO EVIDENCE: nothing enters inventory. Header Time is 30 minutes and there is no time field. Bullet 1 is advice, not a step. The page carries Category:Verification because of a {{verification}} tag on the 'Concerned' dialogue line.

  step 2: Modelled on North Gustaberg (S); see or_branch_unmodelled.

steps.note: 'After confirming the mission with Hieronymus' -- accepting the op.
OR the Gate Sentry in Grauberg (S) at (L-4) the two entries bullet 3 lists. You pick one Bastokan-held Campaign area and the rest of the ladder follows that choice.

escort the 'Reinforcement' NPC here and talk to Jagged Onyx, L.C., who tells you to report back. The Reinforcement wanders off on his own at random or if you get too far away -- Concerned runs back to the Gate Sentry, Combative runs a random path, Impatient heads roughly for the outpost -- and you regain control by talking to him. On the Grauberg (S) branch the destination is Polished Fang, L.C. at (I-8) instead.
the official report. Bullet 7: 'After talking to Hieronymus, the mission is complete.'

THIS OP HAS NO PLACE IN IT, and that is the honest reading rather than a gap. Bullet 1 tells you to WAIT until a Yagudo-held territory comes under campaign battle; its sub-bullet says that means 'all beastman controlled territories in The Aragoneu Front and The Sarutabaruta Front'. Those two are FRONTS -- groupings of zones, and the wiki links them as their own pages -- not zone names, and which zone is eligible changes with the campaign map from hour to hour. So steps 2 and 3 carry zone null and target {none, null}: there is no single place to point at, and inventing one would put a marker somewhere the battle may not be. No marker is drawn from a null name, so the zone-inheritance hazard does not bite here.

THE COMPLETION TEST IS UNOBSERVABLE. Bullet 3: you are rewarded 'after earning over 1500 experience points between combined battles', and the page's own sub-bullet immediately undercuts the number -- 'Reward was not received after earning 1250 experience points, but somewhere between there and 2210' -- while the wikitext hangs a {{verification}} tag on the 1500. Experience earned is not visible to the addon and the page does not agree with itself about the threshold, so it stays in the note. Flagged count_unobservable. That uncertainty is a genuine page problem, not just an unmodellable gate.

NO MONSTERS ARE NAMED, so mobs is [] on the fight step -- a campaign battle names no specific target on this page and I will not put a string in a field that becomes a live marker key.

THE OP ENDS AT THE GIVER, and the page says so: bullet 4, 'Speak to Emhi Tchaoryo to receive your allied note reward and complete the campaign op.'

Notes[1] -- you fail if you join a campaign that does not fit the criteria, or perhaps if you do no damage or healing -- is a warning, not a step, and is itself tagged {{Verification}} in the wikitext. Header Time is empty: unknown, not 'none'. No evidence: nothing enters inventory.

HOW THIS PAGE IS LAID OUT. In the wikitext the walkthrough is one bullet followed by three headed lists; the renderer numbers every list entry as a top-level bullet, so [3]-[6] are Gate Sentries, [7]-[10] are ??? positions and [11]-[14] are Campaign NPCs, while the connective lines ('List of Gate Sentries:', 'Check the ??? to obtain the Key Item "Campaign Supplies".', 'Once you've arrived at the Campaign NPC...', 'After talking to Rasdinice, the mission is complete.') render indented under whichever numbered line precedes them. Those headings are labels, not names, and the closing two sentences are steps that happen to sit under [14].

THE AREA CHOICE IS AN OR AND IS NOT MODELLED. Four areas are offered, each with a matched sentry / ??? / destination triple: East Ronfaure (S) (J-11 / I-11 / H-8), Vunkerl Inlet (S) (E-7 / G-6 / G-10), Jugner Forest (S) (F-5 / F-8 / H-8 or I-8), Batallia Downs (S) (F-8 / G-8 / J-8). You do one. `group` means 'do all of these in any order' and would be false, so I modelled the East Ronfaure (S) triple -- first listed, and the area adjacent to Southern San d'Oria (S) -- and put the rest in the step notes. Flagged or_branch_unmodelled. All four zone names already carry the (S) suffix on the page, so nothing needed normalising.

THE SUPPLIES ARE THEMSELVES A BRANCH, AND THAT ONE IS MODELLED. Bullet 2's sub-bullets say the Gate Sentry will EITHER hand you the Campaign Supplies directly, or send you to recover cargo abandoned en route (the ???), or hand them over with a warning to avoid all confrontation. So the ??? rung is conditional: optional=true. Its evidence is the [KI] Campaign Supplies, which is right in both branches -- holding the key item means the recovery is behind you however you got it -- and the key item is evidence on this step only, so nothing can jump the mark. Flagged or_branch_modelled.

THE DESTINATION HAS NO NAME. [11] is bare: 'East Ronfaure (S): (H-8)'. The prose calls it 'the Campaign NPC', which in the wikitext is the category link [[:Category:Campaign NPC|Campaign NPC]] -- a category, not an NPC -- and 'List of Campaign NPCs:' is a heading. Neither is a name, and any string in target.name becomes a live marker key with nothing validating it, so step 4 is {none, null} with the zone and grid recorded. Flagged generic_npc_name and unnamed_target. Unlike Vanguard-X II (B), this page names no destination NPC in ANY of its four areas.

THE GIVER'S NAME. The closing prose calls him 'Sir Rasdinice' once and 'Rasdinice' once; the header field is 'Rasdinice', and that is what I wrote -- the honorific is how the Campaign NPC addresses him, not part of the name.

Header Time is empty: unknown, not 'none'.
